reason: Assessed both alerts: alert-1 (java/xss) and alert-2 (java/sql-injection) both show user input reaching vulnerable sinks. For java/xss, the header value flows through URL decoding, list manipulation, and finally to the SQL string which is reflected in HTML output via encodeForHTML, but the XSS is still present because the SQL string itself (which includes user input) is part of the HTML output. For java/sql-injection, the header value reaches the SQL query construction directly through the same path. Both alerts are exploitable as the user input reaches the sinks without effective neutralization.
